title: Suleymaniye Mosque, Istanbul
summary: The Suleymaniye Mosque in Istanbul was built for the Ottoman sultan Suleiman the Magnificent by the chief architect Mimar Sinan. Inscriptions show construction began in 1550 and the complex opened for service on 15 October 1557. Anadolu Agency gives its main dome as 26.50 m across and 53 m high.

uncertainty.note: Construction began in 1550 and most of it was finished in 1557, when the mosque was inaugurated (Loyola University Chicago exhibit, citing inscriptions); Anadolu Agency gives 15 October 1557 for the opening of the complex. End is the present.

where.historical_name: Süleymaniye mosque and külliye, Istanbul, Ottoman Empire under Sultan Suleiman

importance.justification: Anadolu Agency calls the complex an embodiment of Suleiman's power and Mimar Sinan's genius; the mosque was Sinan's largest at completion (Loyola exhibit).

reviewer_note: Outline only; no model written. The only metre figures opened are in Anadolu Agency (journalism): dome 26.50 m across and 53 m high; the brief wants UNESCO, heritage-body, museum, university or scholarly pages for the pair, and the Loyola page gives the dome only in cubits (36) with no height. Sources seen only in search snippets gave 26.2, 27.25 and 27.5 m for the diameter and 49-53 m for the height, so the dome diameter is disputed. The MIT Dome record was not reachable.
